about: Where a line marks a footnote (`^[words]`), and the words of each, as the parser (`engine/notes_markdown.py`), the plain reader (`engine/notetext.py`) and the Notebook (`lib/notes/footnotes.js`) all read it: brackets balance, a backslash escapes, code is skipped, and one never closed or holding nothing stays text.

cases.line: The strait was open to both,^[The 1921 text calls it a “common passage”.] for most of the century.
notes: The 1921 text calls it a “common passage”.

cases.line: A note with a link^[See [the treaty](https://example.org/treaty) and [sic] there.] in it.
A note naming a record^[About [[entity:abc|the port]].] in it.
A bracket escaped inside^[one \] two] counts.
A bracket in code inside^[one `]` two] counts.
A caret ^ alone, and a link [words](https://example.org) are no notes.
